memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "On the altar he burned the fat, the kidneys and the long lobe of the liver from the sin offering, as the LORD commanded Moses; the flesh and the hide he burned up outside the camp." - Lev 9:10-11 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
As the LORD commanded Moses. That phrase has now appeared repeatedly across these chapters, and it will keep appearing.

Scripture is not usually repetitive without reason. This refrain is building something — a portrait of a nation doing exactly what God said, step by careful step. It is the calm before chapter 10, where two men will do what God did not command, with terrible consequences.

For now, the note is positive. Aaron obeyed.

There is a quiet beauty in obedience that nobody applauds. Aaron burned the fat as instructed. He carried the remains outside the camp as instructed. No improvisation, no shortcuts, no adding personal flourishes to make it more meaningful.

Our age prizes authenticity and self-expression, sometimes above faithfulness. But God has never asked us to improve on His instructions. He has asked us to trust them.

Samuel put it memorably to a king who had adjusted God's commands to suit himself: To obey is better than sacrifice, and to heed is better than the fat of rams (1 Sam 15:22).

God's way, done God's way, is enough.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I ever adjust God's instructions to make them more comfortable or more impressive?
2. Where is God asking simple obedience from me right now?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, keep me from improving on Your instructions. Give me the humility to do what You have said, the way You have said it. Amen.
